findings.what: LETTER-WINDOW BLIND GAP (R16-A1 (4)). A class-C letter counts as pre-registered if 'the last poll.log header' at logging shows both refs PENDING. The poller writes a header every ~600 s. A score can therefore land in the up-to-10-min gap after that header while the user can already see it on Kaggle's My Submissions page, and the letter would still count as pre-registered. The same gap applies to the R16-A1 (5) rule 'variant not back by the first 43/44 terminal header'. The mechanical stakes are only the label (a late letter is still allowed as USER DECISION AFTER SCORE), but this is the integrity clause the whole class-C table rests on. The fix tightens the rule and is still pre-score.
findings.action: Append one dated line before the first 43/44 terminal header (practically by ~12:15Z; quote the current header): 'R16-A1 (4) clarification (tightening, pre-score): a letter counts as pre-registered only if the last header BEFORE its logged time AND the first header AFTER it both show 56598763 and 56598765 PENDING. Otherwise it is USER DECISION AFTER SCORE. Alternatively, take one ListSubmissions read right after logging the letter and require both PENDING in that read; log the read.' No other change.

findings.what: BLANKET-YES RE-TICK AMBIGUITY (R16-A1 (2) x (5)). R16-A1 (5) reads a blanket yes as 'E10 v2 yes, exp70b yes, class C allowed with the variant pending'. R16-A1 (2) has two branches: 'exp70b letter AND (b)/(c) letter before the read -> one re-tick after the read', and 'only the exp70b letter -> re-tick right after it'. A blanket yes is neither, because the variant is pending. If the session takes the second branch, it re-ticks at once (untick 56563521, tick 56592350), and a (b) answer then needs a second re-tick. Worse, R16-A1 (1) makes the (b) partner #37 unless the letter names exp70b explicitly. So a blanket yes followed by '(b)' yields {V*_C, #37} and silently drops exp70b one message after the user said yes to it. The checklist does ask for the (b) partner, but no default is set for the case where the user answers only '(b)'.
findings.evidence: CONTEXT l.2884-2887 (composition), l.2893-2897 (re-tick), l.2906-2913 (parsing). round16/report.json R16-A8 (i) says 'if a class-C (b)/(c) letter is pending or allowed, one re-tick after the 43/44 read'. R16-A8 (i) therefore already hints at the fix, but it is not in CONTEXT.
findings.action: Add to the same pre-score line as PC17-02: 'A blanket yes (or any letter that allows class C with the variant pending) counts as a pending (b)/(c) letter for R16-A1 (2): exactly one re-tick, after the 43/44 read. If no V*_C exists, that re-tick is {exp70b, #38}. If V*_C exists and the user said yes to exp70b but named no (b) partner, the checklist asks "(b) partner: #37 or exp70b?" and nothing is re-ticked until the answer comes (by 29 Sep 18:00Z; no answer -> {exp70b, #38}, i.e. (a) with the user's exp70b yes).' This is procedural: no new eligibility, no file change.
